title: US Opens Drone and Anti-Drone Technology Market to Mexico to Combat Drug Trafficking
author: SinEmbargo Newsroom
content:
_This article by the SinEmbargo newsroom originally appeared in the[August 16,
2026 edition of SinEmbargo](https://www.sinembargo.mx/4855473/eu-abre-a-
mexico-el-mercado-de-drones-y-tecnologia-antidrones-para-combatir-al-narco/)._

**Mexico City, August 16 (SinEmbargo).—** Mexico will be able to access the
market of the United States (US) military to buy drones and systems capable of
detecting or countering unmanned aircraft, as part of a new security
cooperation agreement to combat drug trafficking.

Thanks to the agreement, Mexico's Defense Ministry will have access to the
digital marketplace of the US armed forces to explore unmanned aerial systems
and anti-drone technology.

The US Ambassador to Mexico, Ronald Johnson, reported this Sunday that the two
countries signed a Declaration of Intent during the visit to Mexico of the US
Army Secretary, Daniel Driscoll.

According to Johnson, the understanding seeks to expand Mexico's capabilities
through new technologies and tools for its security and defense operations.

![Systems designed to detect and counter unmanned
aircraft](https://mexicosolidarity.com/wp-
content/uploads/2026/08/2026-08-16-us-mexico-drones-market-drones.jpg)The
agreement also includes systems designed to detect and counter unmanned
aircraft. Photo: X/@USAmbMex

**" Our defense cooperation continues to strengthen. During Driscoll's visit,
the United States and Mexico's Defense Ministry signed a Declaration of Intent
to strengthen our strategic and operational capabilities through defense
innovation and new technologies," he stated.**

Access to this equipment takes on relevance amid the use of drones by criminal
groups in various parts of the country, since the aircraft serve for
surveillance and tracking, and detecting them is another challenge for the
authorities.

With the new agreement, the Defense Ministry will be able to consult the
offerings of the US Army's digital marketplace and look for systems to
identify and counter unmanned aircraft.

Anti-drone technology is designed to counter this threat, since the system can
detect an aircraft, track its trajectory, and act to prevent it from
continuing to operate.

Ambassador Johnson noted that these tools will allow Mexico to reinforce its
capacity to combat criminal groups and address the security challenges that
both countries share.

**" This technology will strengthen our capacity to combat the cartels and
confront our shared security challenges," he expressed.**

Although the agreement opens the door to these acquisitions, **it is still not
known what equipment Mexico will choose, how much it will buy, or when it will
incorporate it into the Defense Ministry 's operations.**
